# Results — Study 860 (Accounting Conservatism, C-Score)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — a simplified
**Penman-Zhang / Basu conservatism score** (estimated reserves ÷ (net) operating assets)
predicts forward returns. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py`
to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the partial
current month is dropped). Prices fingerprint `5506b659db08` (yfinance daily adjusted closes);
events cache = 1,669 (ticker, filing) rows.*

Stamp: as-of 2026-06-30 · Fingerprint `5506b659db08`

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Universe | **37** deep-history US **non-financial** large filers that tag reserve/allowance accounts on EDGAR (from a fixed 42-name basket; current survivors) |
| Signal source | SEC EDGAR XBRL `companyconcept`: `AllowanceForDoubtfulAccountsReceivableCurrent` + `InventoryValuationReserves` + `DeferredTaxAssetsValuationAllowance` (summed, whichever disclosed); `Assets`, `Cash`, `Liabilities`, `LongTermDebt` for NOA; `NetIncomeLoss` for ROA. De-duplicated on period end, earliest filing kept |
| Panel | **1,669** reserve-disclosing quarters, period ends **2008-09-27 → 2026-05-31**, stamped with the **10-Q/10-K filing date** (point-in-time; no look-ahead) |
| Prices | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, 42 names, sliced to 2026-06-30 |
| Primary signal | `cscore` = (Σ tagged reserves) ÷ Assets — the coarse reserve-intensity C-score; median **0.34%**, mean **0.98%** of assets |
| Primary test | calendar-time monthly long-short: rank fresh signals into **terciles**, **long high-conservatism / short low**, earn **next** month's return (one execution lag); decisive stat = **Newey-West (6-lag) t** |
| Costs | one-way × NAV × monthly turnover on both legs + annualised borrow on the short leg |

**Coverage caveat (first-class).** Reserve/allowance accounts are irregularly tagged — most
names disclose only the allowance for doubtful accounts, and only in some years — so the reserve
total is a **floor** on true estimated reserves, and the C-score is a *coarse* proxy for the
Penman-Zhang construct (which adds LIFO, R&D and advertising reserves we cannot recover from
XBRL). Only **42%** of events carry the full set needed for the cleaner NOA denominator. No
survivorship correction: the basket is current survivors — named on the Signal axis.

## Headline — the forward-return long-short (does conservatism predict returns?)

Monthly rebalanced tercile long-short on `cscore`, one execution lag, 2009-09 → 2026-06
(**202 months**, avg cross-section 28.5 names):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| long-short mean | **+4.0 bps/month** (+0.49%/yr, gross) |
| one-sample *t* | +0.21 |
| **Newey-West (6-lag) *t*** | **+0.22** |
| Sharpe (gross, ann.) | 0.05 |
| monthly hit rate | 49% |
| long leg / short leg | +152.4 / +148.4 bps/month |
| growth of \$1 (gross) | ×1.005 over 202 months |

The long-short is **economically and statistically indistinguishable from zero** (NW *t* =
+0.22, gross ~+0.5%/yr — a flat line, \$1 → \$1.005 over 17 years). And it is **not robustly
right-signed**: a staleness-120 variant flips **negative** (−9.4 bps/month, NW *t* = −0.43), and
the cleaner **NOA-scaled** signal `reserves/NOA` is a dead null (+0.6 bps/month, **NW *t* =
+0.02**, n = 194 months). Whatever direction you read, this tape sees no conservatism return
premium.

## Cross-check — pooled event drift (tercile sort by C-score)

Bucket all (ticker, filing) events by `cscore`; top-minus-bottom forward drift, entered one day
after the filing:

| horizon | n | top | bottom | long-short | one-sample *t* | win | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 21 d (≈1 m) | 1,667 | +1.40% | +1.47% | **−0.07%** | −0.17 | 49% | 0.57 |
| 63 d (≈1 q) | 1,646 | +3.57% | +4.26% | **−0.68%** | −0.91 | 49% | 0.83 |
| 126 d (≈2 q) | 1,615 | +6.55% | +7.91% | **−1.36%** | −1.31 | 48% | 0.92 |

If anything the drift runs **the wrong way**: high-conservatism names *under*-perform low ones by
−1.36% over two quarters (though only *t* = −1.31, insignificant). The tercile means are
**non-monotone** (63 d: +4.26% / +2.57% / +3.57% low→high), and the label-shuffle placebo *p*
sits at **0.57 → 0.92** — a random tercile split beats the real long-short **most of the time**,
exactly because the real one is (weakly) negative. There is **no forward-return sort** in this
signal, in the claimed direction or any other.

## Era split — no regime rescues it

Calendar long-short, split at 2016-01-01:

| era | months | mean | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2009-2015 | 76 | +17.8 bps | +0.55 |
| 2016-2026 | 126 | −4.3 bps | −0.20 |

The **sign flips** across eras and neither half clears the bar. There is no stable, certifiable
positive to find.

## The mechanism check — is the accounting even conservative? (Basu asymmetric timeliness)

Pooled Basu (1997) regression of quarterly ROA on the contemporaneous return $R$, a bad-news
dummy $D=\mathbb{1}[R<0]$, and their interaction (n = 1,607 events, tails trimmed):

$$\text{ROA} = a + b_1 R + b_2 D + b_3\,(D\cdot R)$$

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| good-news slope $b_1$ | +0.006 |
| **asymmetry $b_3$** (bad-news incremental) | **+0.025** |
| *t* ($b_3$, iid-pooled) | **+1.67** |
| R² | 0.005 |

The asymmetry coefficient is **positive** ($b_3 = +0.025$) — earnings load a little more heavily
on bad news than good, the Basu signature of conservatism — but it is only **mildly significant**
(*t* = +1.67, pooled across clustered filings) and the regression explains almost nothing (R² =
0.5%). So the panel is **at most weakly conservative** on this coarse quarterly measure. The
reserve-intensity C-score is a noisy proxy for a real-but-faint property, and that property does
**not** translate into a return edge.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic price + C-score panel with a TUNABLE planted relation (high-conservatism names
drift up); no network. Detector = the primary calendar long-short NW *t*.

| world | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **12 seeds** | mean **+0.47** (sd 0.76), \|t\| ≥ 2 in **0/12** seeds |
| planted edge = 0.15 (seed 860) | **+26.57** (mean +1057.5 bps/month) |

The detector averages ≈0 on the null (zero crossings of \|t\| = 2 in twelve HAC *t*'s) and lights
up hard on a planted relation. The real-tape NW *t* = +0.22 is therefore a genuine null, not a
broken pipeline. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of a real-tape
stamp.)*

## Tradability — the timer

Calendar long-short net of one-way costs × turnover (both legs) + short-leg borrow (monthly
turnover ≈ 0.21):

| cost (one-way) | borrow (ann.) | net mean | ~ann. | Newey-West *t* | Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 10 bps | 50 bps | −4.3 bps/mo | −0.51%/yr | −0.24 | −0.05 |
| 20 bps | 100 bps | −12.5 bps/mo | −1.51%/yr | −0.70 | −0.16 |

There was nothing to charge costs against — the gross edge is already zero — and net of realistic
friction the book **loses money**. No paycheck.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The forward-return long-short is a **flat null** (primary NW *t* = +0.22,
  gross +0.5%/yr, \$1 → \$1.005 over 17 years) and, worse for the claim, **not even robustly
  right-signed**: the pooled event drift runs **negative** at every horizon (−0.07% / −0.68% /
  −1.36%, placebo *p* up to 0.92), the staleness-120 variant is −9.4 bps (NW *t* = −0.43), the
  NOA-scaled signal is a dead +0.02 *t*, and the sign flips across eras. The claimed
  "conservatism return premium" does not appear on this tape.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Zero gross edge; net of 20 bps + 100 bps borrow the long-short is
  **−1.5%/yr** (NW *t* = −0.70, Sharpe −0.16). Nothing to trade.
- **"Is the accounting conservative?" — SUGGESTIVE (gray).** The Basu asymmetry is **positive
  but faint** ($b_3 = +0.025$, *t* = +1.67, R² = 0.5%). The panel is at most mildly conservative
  on a coarse quarterly measure — a real-but-weak property that a thin XBRL reserve proxy
  captures poorly and that, in any case, buys **no return predictability**. Real (faint)
  accounting phenomenon, no alpha in the stock.
